answer.evidence: Both rails are drawn mostly as vertical corrugated faces. Column x=4 shows a light strip at rows 3-4 and x=8 shows a light pixel at row 3, then rust and grey face rows down to a dark outline at row 8. The lower rail starts with only a 1-row light pixel at row 9 (x=8) and has no light band at x=4, so it has no top band, no consistent front-edge line and no eave shadow. The post (x=11) has a 2-row light cap at rows 0-1 and then a vertical face with no top surface. The tops of both rails are only 1-2 row rims, so the object reads as a front elevation, not as rail tops seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is small in the board, so I leaned on the measured facts and checked them against the picture. It has 18 visible tones per 16x16 tile, level with prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20) and well above prop-hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a tint (dark brown beside the wood post, dark red-brown beside the rusty metal) rather than a near-black sticker line. By eye, the rails show a few lightness steps with corrugation ridges and rust or grain variation, and the wooden post is shaded separately. I count about 5 steps on the main ramp against about 6 on the references. It is slightly simpler than the stall and well but does not look thinner or flatter than the hedge or bench references.

The main body reads as three_quarter because the upper rail shows a real top, but the lower rail is weak, so not every major part has a top.
